papers.summary: Defines behavioral rate as the serialized adapter size needed to retain a specified share of held-out fine-tuning gain. Reports that LoRA compressibility varies across frozen base models and that data-measured correction spectra rank rates within a base model.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses whether low-rank compression preserves acquired behavior, rather than merely reconstructing weights.

evidence.quote: the smallest serialized size of a compressed adapter that, once reloaded into the frozen base model, retains a fixed fraction of its held-out fine-tuning gain
fine-tuning compressibility is a property of the dataset--receiver pair rather than of the dataset alone

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Proposes an SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer for LoRA. In reported mixed-domain sweeps, it improves mean Wiki perplexity against unpenalized LoRA at tested ranks of at least 16.
papers.relevance: Direct match for spectral regularization, effective rank, and language-model fine-tuning. Cross-method comparisons are not parameter-count matched.

evidence.quote: our main method adds a simple, stable, differentiable, and SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer to the language-modeling loss.
Comparisons across adapter parameterizations are based on each method’s published or default hyperparameters and are not parameter-count matched

papers.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

papers.summary: Analyzes matrix-factorization dynamics under finite-depth Newton-Schulz updates and shows that the number of steps can change early rank selection and bypass a gradient-flow stationary point.
papers.relevance: Directly connects Muon-style approximation depth to rank formation during optimization.

evidence.quote: the number of Newton-Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training

papers.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle

papers.summary: Tracks LoRA update spectra and subspaces in supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, reporting different spectral concentration and rotation dynamics.
papers.relevance: Direct evidence on how training regimes affect singular-value spectra and low-rank update geometry.

evidence.quote: RL concentrates the spectrum at every learning rate, while SFT expands it at moderate learning rates
RL rotates the singular subspaces much faster than SFT at small learning rates

papers.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

papers.summary: Characterizes the normal space inaccessible to standard LoRA factor gradients and uses its singular directions to motivate rank expansion.
papers.relevance: Direct match for LoRA optimization geometry and adaptive rank selection.

evidence.quote: their unobservable subspace coincides with the normal space of the low-rank manifold
leading normal singular directions yield the locally optimal rank expansion

papers.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA

papers.summary: Distinguishes stable rank from fixed-energy rank in language-model updates and reports measurements of OLMo-2-7B spectra and post-training step directions.
papers.relevance: Clarifies which rank statistic is informative when judging update compressibility.

evidence.quote: three proximal policy optimization (PPO) attention updates have stable ranks of 9.6-18.3 but require 532-1,222 singular components to capture 80% of their energy

papers.title: Spectral Rank and Step-Direction Dynamics in Language-Model Post-Training

papers.summary: ResQAdam retains a BF16 momentum and uses low-rank Adam coordinates plus a residual sign update for quantization-aware training. In the reported hardware comparison, optimizer-state memory falls by 71.3%–73.2%, total peak memory by 15.3%–19.5%, and throughput by 0.6%–1.4% versus AdamW.
papers.relevance: Strong measured quality, memory, and throughput evidence for low-rank optimizer-state compression, specifically in QAT.

evidence.quote: Total Peak Memory (GB) 33.33 / 28.24 ( ↓ \downarrow 15.3%) 43.93 / 37.19 ( ↓ \downarrow 15.3%) 99.14 / 79.77 ( ↓ \downarrow 19.5%) Throughput (# token/s) 29.36k / 28.94k ( ↓ \downarrow 1.4%) 18.31k / 18.19k ( ↓ \downarrow 0.6%) 9.64k / 9.56k ( ↓ \downarrow 0.8%)
All experiments utilize the Basic QAT framework with a W4A4G128 quantization configuration and a context length of 4096.

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

papers.summary: HiLo synchronizes distributed LoRA post-training through compressed gradients and optimizer replay; its Spar compressor combines spectral truncation, adaptive rank allocation, and error feedback.
papers.relevance: Connects training rank to communication cost and learning quality in a distributed setting.

evidence.quote: decouple training rank from communication cost
maintains learning quality close to full synchronization while transmitting as little as 1.6% of the adapter bytes

papers.title: Train High, Ship Low: Efficient LoRA Synchronization for Distributed On-Policy Post-Training

papers.summary: FP4Quant compresses communication in model-parallel LLM training. Its abstract reports up to 1.56× end-to-end throughput improvement over BF16 on H100 with Qwen-7B, while noting a quality tradeoff.
papers.relevance: Covers the profile’s communication, throughput, and model-quality tradeoffs beyond low-rank methods.

evidence.quote: Experiments on NVIDIA H100 GPUs with Qwen-7B demonstrate up to 1.56$\times$ end-to-end throughput improvement over BF16, revealing a trade-off between throughput and model quality.

papers.title: FP4Quant: Efficient 4-Bit Communication Compression for Model-Parallel LLM Training

papers.summary: Analyzes frozen-factor federated LoRA as a rank-dependent stochastic approximation to full fine-tuning and proposes periodically resampling the frozen factor.
papers.relevance: Relevant to rank-dependent LoRA convergence and communication, though its federated setting may not transfer to ordinary fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: the adaptation rank $r$ directly governs the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the perturbed gradients
reduces both computational and uplink communication overheads by 50\%

papers.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA

papers.summary: LIRA reallocates LoRA ranks using estimated local loss perturbations from recent factor movements under a second-order approximation.
papers.relevance: Offers a loss-based alternative to geometric rank expansion for low-rank adaptation.

evidence.quote: LIRA scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of the local loss perturbation associated with its recent LoRA-factor movements under a second-order approximation

papers.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: SaMA proposes a Kronecker-product-based PEFT parameterization intended to reduce LoRA’s optimization invariances and achieve higher effective rank per parameter budget.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization geometry and rank capacity in low-rank alternatives.

evidence.quote: its invariance manifold induces flat directions in the loss landscape, creating an optimization bottleneck for adaptive optimizers
its effective rank scales only linearly with the parameter budget

papers.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product

papers.summary: DictLLM compresses pretrained LLM weights using SVD-derived shared dictionaries, sparse layer coefficients, refinement, and quantization without further training.
papers.relevance: A post-training weight-compression comparator for the goal of preserving quality under low-rank factorization; it does not test training for compressibility.

evidence.quote: directly obtained from a pre-trained model without further training
shared dictionaries via singular value decomposition (SVD) of input-scaled weight matrices

papers.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels

papers.summary: Studies how pretraining, noisy-label supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning interact in an analytical multistage model, with a reported OLMo-2 1B observation.
papers.relevance: Covers the explicitly stated secondary interests in noisy supervision and compute allocation, although most analysis uses a simplified model.

evidence.quote: Better pretraining also reduces sensitivity to noisy supervision.
SFT initialization shortens the initial RL plateau induced by sparse rewards, an effect we also observe in OLMo-2 1B on GSM8K.

papers.title: An Analytical Model of Compute-limited Multistage Training Pipelines

papers.summary: MobileSpec proposes forward-only on-device LLM specialization by training block-spectral coordinates of pretrained weights, motivated by the reported geometry of RLVR updates.
papers.relevance: Links spectral weight parameterization to memory-constrained adaptation, though not to pretraining.

evidence.quote: backpropagation is prohibitive in memory
training only the block-spectral coordinates of pretrained weights

papers.title: Training Specialist LLMs on Your Phone: Forward-Only Optimization via Block-Spectral Coordinates

limitations: Most selected findings are supported only by abstracts; comparative controls and detailed costs remain unverified except where inspection passages are cited.
ResQAdam’s reported peak-memory and throughput comparison is for specified QAT settings on one H200, not general LLM pretraining.
The supplied corpus contains no comparably supported research-digest-agent selection.
Code availability and reproducibility were not verified; X analysis was disabled.
